light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a helper with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered workroom or estate sale house background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the window a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, age spots and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes with real creases. People are caught mid-action, unposed. Daylight from the window on the left plus the ceiling light.
look: Ordinary handheld video filmed by a helper with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural older hands; she moves naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

anchors.prompt: Same workroom, same moment of the day. Hazel, a 69-year-old woman with grey hair loosely pulled back with a few stray strands, thin wire-rimmed reading glasses, small silver drop earrings, a faded blue denim button-up shirt with the sleeves rolled up to the forearms, natural older skin with lines and age spots sits at the worn wooden worktable of her appraisal workroom: white painted board walls, a tall window on the left, a dark wood china cabinet and an old dresser, open shelves with silver teapots and old jewelry boxes behind her, a white magnifier lamp on a swing arm, a pair of white cotton gloves on the worn wooden worktable. A small shiny silver cream pitcher stands on the table in front of her next to the white cotton gloves, and she talks to the camera with one hand open, warm and direct. Medium shot from about one and a half meters, her upper body and the table in frame, the shelves of silver teapots behind her. She wears the same faded blue denim shirt with rolled-up sleeves, the same thin wire-rimmed reading glasses and small silver drop earrings, grey hair loosely pulled back.

A few seconds later, same place: she has picked up the small silver cream pitcher and holds it up beside her face toward the camera in one hand, pointing at it with the index finger of the other hand, eyes wide behind her glasses and mouth open mid-word, surprised and amused. She wears the same faded blue denim shirt with rolled-up sleeves, the same thin wire-rimmed reading glasses and small silver drop earrings, grey hair loosely pulled back.

Same place a few seconds later: she holds the little silver pitcher lower, tilted toward the camera, and taps a tiny round white price sticker on its side with one fingertip, a dry, unimpressed look over the top of her glasses, one eyebrow raised. She wears the same faded blue denim shirt with rolled-up sleeves, the same thin wire-rimmed reading glasses and small silver drop earrings, grey hair loosely pulled back.

Same place a few seconds later: she sets the silver pitcher down on the worktable right in front of the camera and leans in a little over it with both forearms on the table, a knowing, conspiratorial half-smile, as if about to tell a secret. She wears the same faded blue denim shirt with rolled-up sleeves, the same thin wire-rimmed reading glasses and small silver drop earrings, grey hair loosely pulled back.
The same image, unchanged: the two men in work vests are just stepping in through the open front door, the china cabinet on the right untouched.

A second and a half later in the same room: the two men have crossed the living room and the first man is already opening the glass door of the china cabinet on the right, the second right behind him, nothing else in the room has moved.
The same image, unchanged: the older woman's hand holds the little white price sticker just above the silver cream pitcher on the sale table.

A moment later, same table: the little round white price sticker reading $2 is now pressed onto the side of the silver cream pitcher, the woman's hand pulling away toward the right edge, everything else on the table unchanged.
The same image, unchanged: her hands hold the silver cream pitcher upside down under the magnifier lens on the worktable.

A moment later, same worktable: she has tilted the upside-down pitcher closer under the round magnifier lens so its flat bottom with the small stamped hallmark letters fills more of the lens, her thumb beside the stamp.
The same image, unchanged: the small red horseshoe magnet is held a few centimeters above the thin gold chain lying flat on the white cloth.
A moment later, same worktable: the magnet has been lowered until it almost touches the chain, and the gold chain still lies completely flat on the white cloth, unmoved.

clips.text: Forty years I ran estate sales. And every single time, the dealers walk right past the good china... and grab this.
clips.action: She talks to the camera with warm, dry authority, small head movements, and on the last words she picks up the little silver cream pitcher and lifts it beside her face toward the camera, pointing at it, eyes wide. She wears the same faded blue denim shirt with rolled-up sleeves, the same thin wire-rimmed reading glasses and small silver drop earrings, grey hair loosely pulled back.

clips.text: A little silver cream pitcher. Most families put a two dollar sticker on it.
clips.action: She lowers the pitcher a little and taps the tiny white price sticker on its side with one finger, unimpressed, talking to the camera. She wears the same faded blue denim shirt with rolled-up sleeves, the same thin wire-rimmed reading glasses and small silver drop earrings, grey hair loosely pulled back.

clips.text: And that little pitcher? I'll tell you exactly what it sells for.
clips.action: She sets the pitcher down on the table in front of the camera and leans in over it with a knowing half-smile, talking to the camera as if sharing a secret. She wears the same faded blue denim shirt with rolled-up sleeves, the same thin wire-rimmed reading glasses and small silver drop earrings, grey hair loosely pulled back.
